business_scope.primary_industry_name: Global Employer of Record and Cross-Border Contractor Payroll

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Mainland China (People's Republic of China) - incorporating jurisdiction for CN_WFOE_LTD; Taiwan (TW) is the source of cross-strait foreign investment
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Cross-Strait Agreement on Avoidance of Double Taxation and Strengthening of Tax Cooperation (2015)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: People's Bank of China and State Administration for Market Regulation Order No. 3 (2024), Measures for Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing of Market Entities and Beneficial Ownership Information Reporting (effective November 1, 2024); PRC Anti-Money Laundering Law (as amended 2024); PRC Company Law (2023 revision, effective July 1, 2024); Administrative Measures for Enterprise Name Registration (2021); and SAMR Administrative Measures for Foreign-Invested Enterprise Registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (or current business license) of the investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry in the investing shareholder's jurisdiction (for a Taiwan-source investor: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs, Company Registration Office)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path if issued in an Apostille Convention state: notarize the document, then obtain an Apostille from the designated Competent Authority; no PRC consular legalization may follow. Non-member path, including Taiwan: notarize the document, obtain verification from the issuing authority or competent court, and complete cross-strait SEF/ARATS authentication as the consular legalization equivalent; no Apostille may be added.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or authorized corporate service provider in the investing shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarization followed by Apostille only; no consular legalization. Non-member path: notarization followed by competent authority verification and, for Taiwan-source documents, SEF/ARATS authentication; Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and may not be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney authorizing the incorporation of the China WFOE and appointment of its first legal representative and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the investing shareholder, notarized in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: notarize the resolution or PoA, then apostillize; no PRC consular legalization. Non-member path: notarize, verify by the recognized authority, and, if Taiwan-source, submit for SEF/ARATS authentication; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (constitutional documents) of the investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investing shareholder or registrar maintaining the authenticated constitutional instrument
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path if the issuing jurisdiction is a member state: notary certification followed by Apostille only. Non-member path: notary certification followed by consular legalization or, for Taiwan, SEF/ARATS authentication; parallel paths only and no sequential chaining.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter of the investing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing commercial bank in the investing shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path when the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille member: notarized bank officer signature followed by Apostille; no consular legalization. Non-member path: notarized bank signature followed by consular legalization or, for Taiwan, cross-strait authentication through SEF/ARATS; Apostille and consular legalization are parallel and mutually exclusive.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, the WFOE's counsel must run consolidated automated and manual screening of every UBO, shareholder, director, legal representative, senior manager, and authorized signatory against the OFAC SDN and non-SDN consolidated lists, UN Security Council sanctions lists, the European Union's consolidated financial sanctions lists, and domestic lists published by PBOC and China's Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center. All persons must also be screened for PEP status, adverse media, global watchlists, and adverse regulatory actions. Any hit triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and, where appropriate, suspicious transaction reporting to the China Anti-Money Laundering Monitoring and Analysis Center. Screening results must be documented, timestamped, and retained for at least five years after the business relationship terminates.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR National Enterprise Name Self-Declaration and Comparison Service Platform (National Enterprise Registration Online Service), accessible through the local Municipal Market Regulation Administration one-stop enterprise registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory Chinese name must be composed exclusively of Chinese characters; the standard order is administrative division + approved trade name (no fewer than two characters) + industry or business characteristics + the Chinese statutory suffix for a limited liability company. An English name is optional and must correspond to the Chinese trade name through a registered transliteration; pinyin alone is not acceptable as a trade name. Foreign-language trade names may be phonetically transliterated, but the Chinese transliteration must not create a false impression of a prohibited industry, state affiliation, or unlicensed regulated activity.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name self-declaration is rejected, the applicant may submit a written administrative reconsideration application to the immediate higher-level market regulation administration within 60 days of the rejection notice under the Administrative Reconsideration Law, or may directly file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. Before filing, the applicant should use the name comparison module to remove confusingly similar or prohibited tokens, obtain written consent from any prior-name owner if needed, and resubmit the name. The law firm should prepare a legal opinion demonstrating compliance with the 2021 Enterprise Name Registration Measures and, if rejection is based on similarity, compare the relevant trademarks and registered company names, attaching certified copies of priority instruments and any supporting notarized consents.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a China WFOE engaged in ISIC 7810 staffing and EOR services, a virtual office or commercial mailbox is rejected. The local market regulation bureau requires a written lease for a fixed, non-residential premises and conducts location verification; the tax authority requires a physical premises for VAT and general-taxpayer inspection; the human resources and social security authority requires an actual office with employment management equipment for the staffing service license; and banks conduct a physical door-knock visit before opening a corporate account. A virtual address will result in license refusal, tax registration challenges, and bank account rejection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (i) registered premises must be identifiable by signboard, have a lease, occupancy certificate, and business equipment; (ii) staff must be present and able to answer questions on the EOR business; (iii) payroll records, employment service license, and books must be available; (iv) tax registration and social insurance filings must align with the registered address. Quantified risk: moderate - estimated 25% probability of an unannounced inspection in the first operating year if the entity applies for general taxpayer status or a human resources service license; unannounced municipal tax and market regulation inspections occur on a risk-based cycle. High-risk triggers include mailing address conflicts, absence of a signboard, missing lease documents, no employees at the premises, or offsite payroll administration.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official company registration and business license fee (SAMR and local Market Regulation Bureau)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) and local Market Regulation Bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory official fee is charged for initial WFOE incorporation in the PRC; government cost is zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Enterprise name self-declaration and name comparison
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: SAMR National Enterprise Name Service Platform
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No official fee is levied for online name self-declaration and comparison.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Investor corporate documents notarization (certificate of incorporation, good standing, articles, board resolution or PoA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public in the investing shareholder's home jurisdiction
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing notarial tariff based on document pages; approximately USD 100-150 per document.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or consular legalization / cross-strait authentication of investor document bundle
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Designated Competent Authority for Apostilles or PRC consular authority / cross-strait authentication office
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fee per document for five documents; approximately USD 80-120 per document; official PRC government fee may be zero.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Chinese-language translation of all foreign investor documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation firm accepted by the local market regulation bureau
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark of USD 60-90 per 1,000 Chinese characters.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT UBO due diligence, PEP and sanctions screening, and compliance file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: fixed fee for Stage 1 WFOE KYC/AML dossier; hourly billing USD 300-500 if extended.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office physical address and pro-rata lease documentation for first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing commercial rent benchmark for a licensed EOR office premise in a first-tier city, annualized and pro-rated for pre-incorporation.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal engraving (common seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, invoice seal)
Bank reference letter from the foreign investor's bank
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Issuing commercial bank in the investing shareholder's jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Professional handling of tax registration, social insurance registration, and HR license pre-filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party corporate service provider or PRC law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for pre-incorporation registration and regulatory pre-filing work.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (公司法), Articles 98-113 (limited liability company formation, director and officer provisions), Articles 387 and 393 (registration and corporate identity); Foreign Investment Act (外國人投資條例), Articles 7 and 10; Enforcement Rules of the Foreign Investment Act; Employment Services Act (就業服務法), Articles 34-37 (private employment service institution licensing); Occupational Safety and Health Act (職業安全衛生法).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部) - Investment Commission (投資審議司) for foreign investment permission; Department of Commerce (商業發展署) for company incorporation registration; delegated municipal commerce offices for land-based filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) together with the Articles of Incorporation (公司章程), and the Foreign Investment Application (外國人投資申請書).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No general statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Taiwan limited company, but the MOEA Investment Commission verifies capital adequacy for the EOR payroll business plan, and the Ministry of Labor licensing rules require paid-in capital of at least NT$5,000,000 (approx. USD 165,000) if foreign-worker placement is included. The full subscribed capital must be remitted from overseas into a temporary escrow bank account of the company under formation (籌備處專戶), verified by a licensed CPA, and cannot be withdrawn for corporate purposes before the incorporation certificate and the employment service permit are issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF SOLE SHAREHOLDER AND DIRECTORS. The founding shareholder subscribed 100% of the issued capital under the Foreign Investment Act and the Companies Act. RESOLVED: the Articles of Incorporation are approved and adopted. RESOLVED: the registered office is fixed at [address in Taiwan]. RESOLVED: the following officers are appointed effective immediately - Chairperson [name], Director(s) [names], and Compliance Officer [name]. RESOLVED: the Chairperson and Compliance Officer are jointly authorized to file the incorporation with the Ministry of Economic Affairs, open the corporate payroll bank account, and apply for the Ministry of Labor Private Employment Service Institution Permit before the EOR operations commence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (經濟部), Company Registration and Name Reservation Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online application reserving up to five preferred Chinese company names and the English name 'CN WFOE LTD'. Select the business scope code corresponding to ISIC 7810 / NAICS 561330 (HR and EOR services) and pay the NT$300 name-check fee per name. The system rejects identical or confusingly similar names against the national corporate registry and issues a Name Reservation Certificate valid for six months.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form (公司名稱預查申請書)
Proposed Chinese and English company names
Business scope code sheet covering ISIC 7810 / NAICS 561330
Founder identity document (passport or foreign corporate registration certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is queried as confusingly similar, file a supplementary name set through the same portal within 10 working days; if the business scope code is disputed, attach the official MOEA scope definition for human resource placement and request re-classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval (Investment Permit) Under the Foreign Investment Act
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Investment Commission (經濟部投資審議司)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Foreign Investment Application (外國人投資申請書) with the proposed Articles of Incorporation, a business plan covering the global EOR and cross-border contractor payroll model, notarized shareholder identity evidence, and a bank reference. The Investment Commission reviews under Articles 7 and 10 of the Foreign Investment Act, screens for national security and prohibited business lines, and issues a formal Investment Permit, which is the precondition for capital remittance and company registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application form (外國人投資申請書)
Business plan for global EOR and contractor payroll operations
Draft Articles of Incorporation (公司章程草案)
Notarized passport or corporate certificate of the foreign shareholder
Bank reference and capital source statement
Power of attorney appointing the local incorporation agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The Commission issues a written deficiency list; the applicant must cure within 60 days or the application lapses and a fresh filing is required. If the application fails national security screening, submit a revised business scope removing sensitive activities and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Taiwan CPA (會計師) and commercial bank accepting the overseas remittance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary escrow account (籌備處銀行專戶) in the name of 'CN WFOE LTD (in preparation)' at a licensed Taiwan bank. Remit the full subscribed capital approved in the Investment Permit from the overseas parent via SWIFT. The bank issues a deposit certificate; a licensed CPA audits the deposit and issues the Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書) confirming that capital is fully paid before incorporation registration.
required_dossiers: Investment Permit from the MOEA Investment Commission
Temporary escrow account opening form and bank deposit certificate
SWIFT remittance record and source-of-funds declaration
CPA Capital Verification Report (資本額查核報告書)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the remittance due to source-of-funds or KYC queries, provide certified corporate registration, audited financial statements, and the Investment Permit; the escrow balance must be re-verified by the CPA after any correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Registration and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (經濟部商業發展署) via the MOEA One-Stop Online Filing Portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Company Incorporation Registration Application (公司設立登記申請書) with the adopted Articles of Incorporation, the first resolution of the shareholder and directors, the Investment Permit, the CPA Capital Verification Report, the lease agreement for the registered office, and identification of the directors. The system computes the NT$1,000- NT$2,000 statutory registration fee; after review the registry issues the Incorporation Certificate and the unified corporate identity number.
required_dossiers: Incorporation registration application form (公司設立登記申請書)
Adopted Articles of Incorporation (公司章程)
First resolution of the sole shareholder and directors
Investment Permit (投資許可函)
CPA Capital Verification Report
Registered office lease agreement and landlord consent
Identity documents of directors and compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction order, rectify the stated deficiencies within 15 days; if the six-month validity of the name reservation lapses, reserve a new name and re-file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration, VAT Business Registration, and Labor/NHI Employer Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (財政部各地區國稅局), Bureau of Labor Insurance (勞動部勞工保險局), and National Health Insurance Administration (衛生福利部中央健康保險署)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation the MOEA data is automatically transmitted to the tax bureau; complete the Business Income Tax and Uniform Invoice/VAT registration in person or via the e-service portal to obtain the tax certificate and uniform invoicing number; register the company as an employer with the Labor Insurance Bureau and NHI Administration, thereby enabling statutory payroll contributions for future EOR employees.
required_dossiers: Incorporation Certificate and corporate identity number
Tax and business registration application (稅籍登記申請書)
Company seal form and responsible person identity
Office address verification (lease and use certificate)
Labor insurance and NHI employer registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Tax registration data mismatches are cured through the joint tax-registry correction portal within 30 days; late-registration penalties may be mitigated by presenting the automated incorporation date record.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Administration (財政部賦稅署) and regional National Taxation Bureaus (國稅局); official online portals: https://www.etax.nat.gov.tw and https://www.mof.gov.tw
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign enterprise must first obtain approval from the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Company Act for a branch or representative office; upon approval, the Ministry of Economic Affairs issues the Uniform Number (統一編號), which thereafter functions as the TIN. The enterprise must then file tax registration with the local National Taxation Bureau. For cross-border e-commerce or offshore services without a fixed place of business in Taiwan, registration for a tax ID and VAT collection may be completed through the Ministry of Finance's overseas e-commerce seller registration mechanism, with liability to appoint a domestic tax agent where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No general check-the-box election exists. Taiwan applies entity-level taxation to corporate entities. A foreign enterprise with a fixed place of business in Taiwan is taxed as a branch; a foreign enterprise without a fixed place or business agent in Taiwan is subject only to withholding on Taiwan-source income. Taxable-period election for VAT may be monthly or bi-monthly depending on turnover and assessed status. Taiwan's Income Tax Act Articles 43-3 and 43-4 contain hybrid mismatch and anti-avoidance provisions, and Article 43-4 restricts interest deductions on back-to-back loans from foreign related parties; elections under these rules must be documented contemporaneously for transfer pricing and thin-capitalization purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax; 營業稅)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$80,000 average monthly taxable sales for small-scale business exemption purposes; VAT registration is generally mandatory for businesses with fixed premises and monthly sales above NT$80,000, while foreign electronic services suppliers must register for VAT when generating Taiwan-source digital service revenue, regardless of physical presence.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan mandates the Uniform Invoice (統一發票) system. VAT-registered businesses must issue electronic uniform invoices and transmit them to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Platform (電子發票整合服務平台) via an approved electronic-invoice service provider or direct API/M2M transmission, within the statutory filing window after the tax period. Cloud-based e-invoices are digitally archived; there is no per-invoice physical stamping, but real-time electronic submission, encryption standards, and audit trail obligations are enforced. B2B and B2C transmission formats must conform to the Ministry of Finance e-invoice UBL/JSON specifications.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies when exported goods actually leave the customs territory under a valid export declaration and are sold by a VAT-registered Taiwan exporter. Cross-border services, including international transport and services rendered to foreign businesses and used wholly outside Taiwan, qualify as zero-rated export services. An employer-of-record or staffing agency may zero-rate cross-border payroll and administrative services to a foreign client if the place of use and customer affiliation are outside Taiwan; documentary evidence must demonstrate the foreign receiving enterprise and actual offshore use. Services consumed in Taiwan or benefiting a Taiwan-resident recipient remain taxable at 5%, with reverse-charge or withholding obligations for foreign-cross-border suppliers where applicable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or airway bill
Inward remittance certificate or bank foreign-exchange settlement certificate
Commercial invoice and full export sales contract
Electronic uniform invoice or zero-rated invoice evidence
Duty-paid, insurance, inspection, and customs packing lists where applicable
Third-party confirmation of offshore service use for service exports
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau cross-matches customs data, port manifests, VAT returns, and inbound foreign-exchange receipts. Claiming zero-rating on goods or services not actually exported, or failing to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory periods, triggers reassessment of VAT at 5% plus interest and a surcharge under Business Tax Act Articles 51 and 52. Fraudulent zero-rating claims may be penalized up to five times the undercollected tax, and criminal liability for tax evasion under Articles 41 and 52 of the Business Tax Act can lead to imprisonment where fraudulent intent is established. Retrospective examination may extend up to seven years in cases involving deliberately misleading documentation or tax evasion.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC); the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) is the delegated foreign-exchange supervisory authority operating under the PBoC and is the sole regulator for cross-border capital flows, FX registration, and the licensing of FX business conducted by banks in mainland China.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China maintains current-account convertibility under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations, meaning cross-border payments and receipts for trade in goods, services, and legitimate profit remittances are permitted upon submission of authentic underlying documentation and completion of bank-based verification. Capital-account transactions remain subject to a case-by-case registration/approval regime administered by SAFE; foreign direct investment into a WFOE, including a Taiwan-origin capital injection, requires FDI registration with SAFE or a designated bank, followed by the opening of a foreign-currency capital account. Profit repatriation from a CN_WFOE_LTD is routed through the current account only after the annual audit report, corporate income tax settlement, withholding tax clearance (where applicable), and bank review of the board resolution and audited financial statements have been completed; Taiwan-registered shareholders benefit from preferential tax treatment under the ECFA framework but must still comply with the same remittance documentary chain. Dividends remitted to Taiwan are generally permitted once the relevant tax payment certificates are filed with the remitting bank, yet the bank remains responsible for reputational and source-of-funds diligence. In practice, the convertibility bottleneck is documentary integrity rather than exchange-control denial for genuine EOR payroll and service-fee transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: The compulsory surrender of export proceeds has been abolished; there is currently no statutory mandatory conversion ratio for export or service income received by a WFOE. Instead, SAFE requires that goods-trade export proceeds be repatriated into mainland China and banked into the exporter's export-earnings verification account or a current-account FX account; the proceeds may remain in FX unless the enterprise voluntarily elects settlement into RMB. For goods exports, the enterprise must receive the payment within 90 days from the customs declaration date unless a deferred-receipt registration is lodged with SAFE through the goods-trade monitoring system; prepayments received more than 30 days prior to export require advance-receipt reporting. All service-trade receipts generated by the Global EOR and cross-border payroll business must be reported to the bank under the service-trade income and expense declaration code corresponding to ISIC 7810, and must be supported by the underlying EOR service agreement, beneficiary confirmation, and PBOC/SAFE-compliant payment instruction, but no minimum retention or forced conversion timeline applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited (中国银行)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (FDI capital foreign-exchange account and RMB registered capital account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. (招商银行)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (basic deposit account plus current-account FX settlement account)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited (中国工商银行)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (basic RMB deposit and general foreign-exchange account)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for the core treasury function. A global EMI such as Airwallex, Wise, or Currenxie is fully viable for auxiliary cross-border disbursement initiation, but each is classified as a non-bank payment institution rather than a licensed mainland-China depository institution. Such platforms cannot host the WFOE's statutory capital account, cannot perform SAFE FDI registrations, and cannot execute legal-current RMB payroll disbursements that require direct-deposit rails into Chinese bank cards. The WFOE may legally use these fintech platforms only as an instruction front-end; the underlying clearing must settle through a Chinese-licensed partner bank within China. Banks will generally require that the fintech account be identified as a regular sanctioned payment aggregator and that the WFOE's name on the fintech account be identical to its Chinese business license name; otherwise, the account can be rejected at bank onboarding.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person appearance is mandatory. Under current PBoC account-opening rules, at least the legal representative or one board-authorized director of the WFOE must appear in person at the bank counter for the initial KYC interview; video-call verification alone is not accepted for a corporate account opening. For a Taiwan-resident shareholder or director, the physical interview may be conducted at the mainland branch, but the individual must bring an acceptable Taiwan Resident Travel Permit or a passport endorsed with a mainland-issued visa/residence permit. If the ultimate beneficial owner is a Taiwan legal person, certified copies of the ultimate shareholder register must be notarized in Taiwan and, where requested, legalized by the local mainland-authority service center. Banks may permit a second authorized signer to appear alongside the legal representative, but the legal representative must also attend unless an explicit notarized power of attorney, apostilled or legalized in accordance with mainland-Taiwan cross-strait instruments, is provided.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Taiwanese ultimate beneficial ownership combined with a fast-growing cross-border payroll business perceived by the bank as a high-volume fund-transit risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the original business license in the Enterprise Social Credit Code; board resolution designating directors and signatories; notarized certificate of incumbency and shareholding register of the Taiwan investor; passports/Residence Permits of all shareholders; source-of-funds evidence for the initial capital; audited financial statements (or an opening-dormant balance sheet) accompanied by a business-plan memorandum explaining the EOR operating model and confirming full tax-registration status in mainland China.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Average monthly payroll disbursements exceed projected company revenue or show patterns of payments splitting for amounts just below reporting thresholds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply executed Global EOR service agreements with each client company, along with corresponding employment agreements and professional-service contracts with contractors; present a complete monthly payroll register, individual employee/contractor identity documents, tax-withholding filings, and employer social-insurance payment proofs; prepare a bank authorization letter from each client for third-party payroll disbursement; provide an accounting explanation that all fund inflows from clients are recorded under service revenue and not as loans or repayment obligations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: Transactions to Taiwan-based subcontractors or to jurisdictions on the bank's monitoring list, especially where the recipient is not an established operating company.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide detailed vendor/contractor onboarding files: business registration or individual ID for the payee, signed contract or short-term service agreement, invoice or work-completion certificate, tax registration of the beneficiary, and any required customs or cross-border service-trade declaration forms; maintain a permanent repository of every remittance's purpose code and underlying service evidence to allow the bank to execute straight-through checks without hold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire-transfer protocol for Taiwan-investor capital injection: (1) the Taiwan shareholder remits via SWIFT MT103 to the mainland WFOE's FDI capital account, with the referencing field carrying 'INVESTMENT CAPITAL WFOE [Legal Name]' and purpose code '712030 – direct investment foreign exchange settlement'; (2) after receipt by the mainland bank, the FDI registration in SAFE's Capital Account Information System must be updated and the capital transaction reported as 'balance of payments direct investment inflow'; (3) the bank then settles the foreign currency into RMB into the WFOE's RMB registered-capital account, or holds it as FX at the customer's direction; (4) if capital is injected in RMB via cross-border RMB settlement, the remitter must use the PBoC RCPMIS system and open a cross-border RMB capital account. All inbound remittances must match the nominal shareholding percentage stated in the latest FDI registration; any change in equity proportion triggers an updated FDI amendment registration within 30 days.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For the Global EOR payroll and contractor settlement model, outbound flows are classified into (a) domestic payroll — executed via the China National Advanced Payment System (CNAPS) using direct debit/credit transfers on the same-day by the bank, and (b) cross-border contractor/vendor payments — completed through SWIFT MT103 in USD/EUR or through CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) for RMB-denominated payments, using the applicable service-trade purpose code for EOR-related fees. Commercial letters of credit are not typical for payroll processing and should be restricted to cargo-based back-to-back trade finance. The fintech gateway Wise may be engaged as a customer-facing disbursement accelerator, but the underlying settlement currency must be debited from the WFOE's Bank of China or China Merchants Bank account and must pass through a China-licensed counterparty bank; Wise will not be recognized as a legal clearing rail by SAFE. Every outbound salary or vendor payment must be reported under the service-trade declaration system with the relevant invoice, contract, and tax-payment voucher retained on file for no less than five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: RMB FX forwards (yuan-FX deliverable forwards) traded with a licensed onshore bank under a real trade background and within the annual hedging quota
Cross-currency swaps between RMB and USD/TWD/HKD executed for economic hedging of EOR payroll exposures under approved bank counterparty ISDA/CSA documentation
RMB/USD FX options (European-style) with an approved onshore bank and a delivery requirement tied to the underlying service-trade cash flow

stage_5.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder meeting (股东常会) or written resolution of the sole corporate shareholder, adopting the annual financial statements and profit-appropriation plan
stage_5.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance act; the adopted minutes are subsequently filed with the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
stage_5.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for the calendar-year WFOE, on or before 30 June each year
stage_5.delinquency_sanctions: No separate filing fine for a non-public company, but the AGM resolution is a precondition to the statutory accounts filing; continued non-convening allows MOEA to order rectification and, in persistent cases, supports administrative deregistration for failure to maintain good standing

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 20% corporate income tax in Taiwan; a 5% additional tax applies to current-year earnings not distributed within the statutory period, subject to applicable exemptions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax holidays and preferential incentives are activity-specific rather than generally available to EOR businesses. Potential relief may include approved R&D investment credits, qualifying smart-machinery or advanced-technology investment credits, qualified investment incentives under the Act for Promotion of Private Participation in Transportation and other sector laws, and approved innovation or strategic-industry incentives. Incentives require statutory eligibility, advance approvals where applicable, substantiation, and separate filing claims. Payroll pass-through amounts are not automatically deductible merely because they are contractually reimbursed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return; electronically filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance e-filing system operated by the National Taxation Bureau. A company established in Taiwan generally files an annual corporate income tax return for the preceding fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year taxpayer, filing and payment are generally due from May 1 through May 31 of the following year. A taxpayer using a non-calendar fiscal year generally files within the fifth month after fiscal year-end. Extension rules are limited and must be confirmed for the relevant year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unified Business Number, legal name, registered address, fiscal-year period, industry classification, responsible person, accounting currency, and tax-agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Taiwan company reports as a resident enterprise. A non-resident foreign enterprise reports only Taiwan-source income, Taiwan permanent-establishment income, or income otherwise subject to Taiwan withholding or filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report EOR platform fees, recruitment or staffing fees, payroll administration fees, management fees, commissions, and other operating receipts on an accrual basis, subject to the applicable accounting and tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident must allocate Taiwan-source receipts and must not treat Taiwan customer receipts as automatically outside Taiwan tax merely because services are invoiced offshore.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report salaries, statutory social insurance, labor pension contributions, bonuses, employee benefits, and other substantiated personnel costs. Payroll paid on behalf of a customer must be separated from the entity's own service revenue and expenses based on the legally supportable principal-agent analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident cannot deduct Taiwan payroll costs without demonstrating the relevant Taiwan activity, personnel, contractual liability, and source-of-income connection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Cost of services and subcontractor expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report contractor fees, local payroll processing, technology hosting, payment processing, compliance services, and other direct service costs with invoices, contracts, payment evidence, and beneficiary details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to foreign related parties require source, benefit, withholding, transfer-pricing, and documentary analysis. Unsupported pass-through deductions are high-risk.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report deductible depreciation, amortization, rent, professional fees, insurance, travel, marketing, bank charges, and other business expenses in accordance with Taiwan tax law and documentary requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses must be necessary, ordinary, business-related, properly documented, and not personal or shareholder expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose controlled transactions involving services, financing, royalties, software, cost allocations, guarantees, receivables, and other cross-border dealings. Reconcile accounting amounts to the arm's-length analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign related-party payments must be supported by a functional analysis, pricing method, intercompany agreement, benefit evidence, and applicable withholding compliance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile financial statement profit or loss to taxable income, including nondeductible expenses, exempt income, tax depreciation differences, prior-year losses, withholding credits, tax incentives, and undistributed-earnings adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Permanent-establishment profits should be determined using a defensible attribution method and should not be reduced by artificial offshore allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax payable, provisional payments, and credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compute regular corporate income tax, apply eligible credits and prepaid tax, and report the balance payable or refundable. Provisional income tax filings and payments are generally made in September for qualifying taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding tax collected at source may be creditable only where statutory conditions and supporting certificates are satisfied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determine whether current-year earnings remain undistributed after the statutory distribution deadline and compute the 5% additional tax where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders must be separately tested for withholding tax, beneficial ownership, treaty or arrangement relief, and corporate-law distribution requirements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Submit or retain balance sheet, income statement, tax reconciliation, related-party schedules, fixed-asset schedules, loss schedules, withholding certificates, and other required attachments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-language documents may require Chinese translation, certification, authentication, or Taiwan tax-agent support depending on the document and audit request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing, non-filing, underreporting, failure to pay, and failure to retain supporting records may result in tax assessments, interest, administrative fines, denial of deductions, loss carryforward restrictions, and criminal exposure for fraud or evasion. Annual income tax late-filing penalties are generally calculated by reference to tax payable and statutory minimum and maximum amounts; failure to file after notice can produce materially higher penalties. Exact amounts depend on the violation, tax payable, filing status, and current law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Provisional Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Return, filed electronically or through the competent National Taxation Bureau.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed and paid during September for the first six months of a calendar year, subject to statutory exceptions, prior approval, and the taxpayer's filing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the prescribed provisional income base or approved accounting-based calculation for the first half of the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident files only where the relevant Taiwan filing obligation applies; Taiwan-source income subject solely to final withholding is not automatically included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate the provisional tax and credit eligible prepaid amounts and withholding tax where legally permitted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim foreign or Taiwan withholding credits without valid certificates and a corresponding legal entitlement.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or inaccurate provisional filing may generate interest, penalties, assessment by the tax authority, and cash-flow consequences at the annual settlement. Certain qualifying taxpayers may be exempt from provisional filing under statutory conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Business Tax Return, including the Value-Added Tax return filed through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance electronic tax filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed and paid by the 15th day of the month following each two-month VAT period. The standard VAT rate is 5%, subject to zero-rating, exemption, and special rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report taxable sales of EOR administration, payroll processing, platform, recruitment, consulting, and related services supplied in Taiwan or otherwise taxable under Taiwan VAT rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign service supplier must assess Taiwan fixed-business-place, electronic-service, and customer-location rules before treating services as outside Taiwan VAT.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report only transactions satisfying statutory zero-rating or exemption conditions and retain destination, customer, contract, and service-delivery evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border invoicing alone does not establish zero-rating or exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible input VAT supported by uniform invoices, customs documents, and business-use evidence.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Input VAT connected with exempt, private, or unsupported activities may be denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate output VAT less allowable input VAT and report payment or refund position.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Refund claims receive enhanced scrutiny where the business has substantial export, zero-rated, or pass-through characteristics.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing, omitted sales, improper invoice issuance, false invoices, and underpaid VAT may result in supplemental tax, interest, administrative fines, invoice restrictions, input-credit denial, and criminal liability for fraudulent or fictitious transactions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding Tax Statement and Withholding Tax Payment Filing through the Taiwan Ministry of Finance electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Monthly, with annual or event-based reporting for certain income categories
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Tax withheld during a month is generally paid and reported by the 10th day of the following month. Annual withholding statements and certificates are generally issued and filed by the applicable statutory deadline, commonly by January 31 for the preceding calendar year, subject to category-specific rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report recipient name, taxpayer identification number or passport details, address, residency status, beneficial-owner information where required, and payment date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a valid foreign tax identification number, certificate of residence, beneficial-owner representation, and treaty-relief documentation before applying a reduced rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Classify dividends, interest, royalties, professional fees, commissions, salaries, rent, prizes, or other payments and determine whether Taiwan withholding applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments for services performed in Taiwan, Taiwan-use royalties, Taiwan-source interest, and dividends from Taiwan companies require specific source and withholding analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report the gross payment, statutory rate, reduced treaty or arrangement rate where valid, tax withheld, and remittance date.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withholding agents remain liable for under-withheld tax even where the payment recipient provided incorrect information.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Issue the withholding certificate, remit withheld tax, and retain contracts, invoices, residency evidence, approvals, and payment records.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not release gross funds on the assumption that treaty relief will be approved retroactively.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit can make the payer liable for the tax that should have been withheld, interest, administrative fines, and potential criminal sanctions for deliberate concealment, false reporting, or tax evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 21% on dividends distributed by a Taiwan company to a non-resident shareholder, subject to applicable tax treaty relief, approved special rules, and the shareholder's legal status. Dividends paid to a Taiwan-resident individual are generally subject to Taiwan's separate resident taxation mechanism rather than the non-resident withholding rate.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan applies its income tax treaties and arrangements according to the relevant instrument. Before payment, the recipient should provide a valid certificate of tax residence, beneficial-ownership evidence, ownership and holding-period information where relevant, completed payer documentation, and substantive eligibility evidence. The payer should confirm the reduced rate with the competent National Taxation Bureau or follow the applicable withholding-agent procedure. Mainland China and Taiwan do not have a conventional comprehensive bilateral income tax treaty equivalent to a standard treaty network instrument; a mainland China recipient should not claim treaty relief without a specific legally applicable cross-Strait arrangement or domestic rule. Treaty relief does not remove Taiwan-source characterization, beneficial-ownership, anti-abuse, or substance requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties paid to a non-resident are generally subject to 20% withholding; interest is generally subject to 15% for interest on qualifying government bonds, corporate bonds, financial bonds, and certain other qualifying instruments, and 20% for other interest, subject to statutory classifications. Treaty rates may reduce these rates, commonly subject to a treaty ceiling, residence certification, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or anti-abuse provisions, and competent-authority procedures. Payments for software, technology, know-how, trademarks, platform access, data, and bundled services require characterization analysis because royalty and service components can have different source and withholding outcomes.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Taiwan generally requires a Local File when annual net operating revenue and non-operating income reach NT$300 million or when the aggregate annual amount of specified controlled transactions reaches NT$200 million, subject to prescribed exemptions. A Master File is generally required for an enterprise meeting the prescribed large-enterprise threshold, commonly annual revenue of at least NT$3 billion together with relevant cross-border controlled transactions. Country-by-Country Reporting generally applies to an ultimate parent or designated surrogate parent in Taiwan where consolidated group revenue reaches NT$27 billion and the statutory conditions are met. Thresholds and exemptions must be checked for the relevant fiscal year.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other methods consistent with Taiwan transfer-pricing regulations and OECD-based principles where the prescribed methods are not reasonably applicable
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan does not operate a single, standalone UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation regime applicable to all entities. Substance is enforced through transfer-pricing rules, controlled-foreign-company rules, permanent-establishment principles, general anti-avoidance provisions, beneficial-ownership analysis, tax-source rules, business-tax rules, and anti-abuse doctrines. A Taiwan EOR company should maintain real decision-making, appropriately skilled personnel, payroll and operational capability, customer and vendor control, commercial risk assumption, local records, and a defensible delineation between principal, agent, payroll processor, staffing provider, and technology platform. A foreign company cannot avoid Taiwan taxation merely by contracting offshore if its people or dependent agents habitually conclude contracts or perform core services in Taiwan.
eor_specific_transfer_pricing_controls: Benchmark the Taiwan entity's remuneration against its functions, assets, and risks rather than automatically applying a cost-plus mark-up.
Separate employee payroll, statutory benefits, customer funds, platform fees, recruitment fees, and the entity's own margin in the ledger and contracts.
Document whether the Taiwan entity is principal, disclosed agent, undisclosed agent, payroll processor, staffing provider, or limited-risk service provider.
Test intercompany service charges, software royalties, financing, guarantees, cost allocations, and regional management fees for benefit, duplication, withholding, VAT, and deductibility.
Prepare contemporaneous intercompany agreements, invoices, time records, allocation keys, benchmarking, board approvals, and payment evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized Mainland China investment or prohibited ownership
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Mainland China company or Mainland Chinese person directly or indirectly establishes, funds, controls, or acquires a Taiwan business without approval under Taiwan's cross-Strait and foreign investment restrictions, or uses nominees and offshore vehicles to conceal Mainland ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Possible rejection or revocation of investment approval, forced disposal, confiscation or forfeiture of prohibited investment gains, administrative fines, restrictions on business operations, and criminal exposure under applicable cross-Strait investment laws. The amount depends on the statute and conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors, managers, nominees, and beneficial owners may face administrative and criminal liability. Civil restitution and disgorgement may apply. Travel restrictions may be imposed in criminal or enforcement proceedings where legally authorized; imprisonment is fact-dependent and not automatic. Limited liability does not protect persons who personally participate in unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed labor dispatch, staffing, or recruitment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a labor dispatch agency, recruitment agency, or employment service without the required Taiwan license, registration, approval, or permitted business scope; misclassifying dispatched workers as independent contractors or platform users.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Orders to cease, administrative fines, license denial or revocation, labor-law penalties, back-pay and benefit assessments, and potential criminal exposure for serious or repeated violations. Penalty amounts depend on the violated Labor Standards Act, Employment Service Act, or other applicable statute.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and responsible managers may be fined or prosecuted where they ordered, approved, or knowingly tolerated the conduct. The company may remain liable for wages, social insurance, labor pension, tax, and damages. Imprisonment is possible for specified offenses but is not an automatic consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate income tax evasion and false returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing Taiwan-source revenue, fabricating expenses, using sham offshore invoices, misclassifying customer payroll as tax-free pass-through funds, manipulating related-party margins, or submitting false books or returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Supplemental tax, interest, tax-loss denial, administrative penalties, audit adjustments, and criminal prosecution for deliberate tax evasion or fraudulent reporting. Criminal sanctions may include imprisonment and criminal fines under the Income Tax Act and related laws; the precise range depends on the offense and amount involved.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may face criminal liability, civil restitution of unpaid tax and penalties, asset attachment, and restrictions on leaving Taiwan where authorized by procedural law. The corporate veil is not automatically pierced, but fraud, personal participation, commingling, and abuse of the company may support direct liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Issuing or obtaining false uniform invoices, claiming input VAT for nonexistent purchases, omitting taxable service revenue, or routing customer funds through fabricated invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Input VAT denial, supplemental VAT, fines, invoice restrictions, business suspension, and criminal sanctions for fraudulent tax evasion or false invoicing. Criminal exposure may include imprisonment and fines depending on the transaction value and intent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, accounting personnel, and beneficial owners who knowingly participate may incur criminal and civil liability. Restitution and asset preservation are possible. Travel restrictions and detention depend on the criminal process and evidence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, royalties, Taiwan-performed services, salaries, rent, or other Taiwan-source income to non-residents without withholding, under-withholding based on unsupported treaty claims, or failing to remit and report withheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer may be assessed the unwithheld tax, interest, penalties, and administrative fines. Deliberate concealment or falsified withholding certificates can create criminal tax exposure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible officers and withholding agents may be personally liable under applicable tax provisions where they intentionally or negligently fail to perform statutory duties. Civil recovery and enforcement measures may follow; imprisonment is reserved for qualifying criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party payments
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using artificial service fees, royalties, financing charges, cost allocations, or guarantees to shift Taiwan profits without benefit evidence, personnel capacity, comparable support, or contemporaneous documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authority adjustment to arm's-length income, denial of deductions, interest, penalties, withholding tax reassessment, VAT consequences, and potential CFC or anti-avoidance adjustments. Failure to provide required documentation may trigger statutory penalties and adverse estimation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil claims for breach of duty and, where deliberate falsification or evasion is proven, criminal liability. Ordinary transfer-pricing adjustment does not by itself establish criminal conduct or pierce the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining Taiwan personnel, dependent agents, sales staff, payroll operators, or contract-concluding representatives while claiming that all revenue belongs to an offshore principal with no Taiwan taxable presence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Retroactive Taiwan income tax, business tax, withholding tax, interest, penalties, payroll and labor assessments, and possible registration or licensing orders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may face civil and, for intentional concealment, criminal exposure. Personal travel restrictions are possible only under applicable enforcement or criminal procedures; they are not a routine tax consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML, KYC, sanctions, and suspicious payment activity
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting or transferring payroll funds without beneficial-owner verification, using personal or nominee accounts, structuring payments, concealing Mainland China flows, failing to report suspicious transactions, or using payment rails in breach of Taiwan financial regulations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines, enhanced monitoring, account freezing, transaction rejection, license or registration consequences, confiscation, and criminal prosecution under Taiwan AML and financial laws. Penalties vary materially by offense and amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners may face criminal fines, imprisonment, confiscation, civil restitution, asset freezing, and legally authorized travel restrictions. Limited liability does not protect knowing participants or facilitators.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll tax, labor insurance, and pension non-compliance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to register employees, withhold salary tax, enroll workers in labor insurance, contribute to labor pension, or correctly identify the employing entity in an EOR arrangement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Back taxes, insurance and pension contributions, surcharges, labor-law fines, employee compensation, interest, and possible suspension or licensing consequences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible persons may incur fines and civil liability for unpaid wages, contributions, and damages. Criminal liability can arise for intentional withholding, fraud, or repeated unlawful conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Beneficial ownership concealment and corporate veil abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using nominee directors, shell companies, undisclosed related accounts, circular transactions, or commingled funds to conceal the true controller, evade investment restrictions, defeat tax collection, or frustrate creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disregard of the arrangement, tax reassessment, confiscation, fines, dissolution or liquidation measures, transaction invalidation, creditor remedies, and criminal prosecution for fraud, forgery, money laundering, or tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may impose direct civil liability where the company is abused, undercapitalized, commingled, or used for fraud. Directors and controllers may face restitution, asset attachment, criminal fines, imprisonment, and legally authorized travel restrictions.
